title: Elon Musk Says He Feels 'Foolish' Over 2026 Midterm Spending and Clarifies He Is 'Not MAGA'
meta_title: Elon Musk Regrets 2026 Midterm Spending and Declares He Is 'Not MAGA'
meta_description: Billionaire Elon Musk admitted he feels 'foolish' after spending hundreds of millions backing failed GOP midterm candidates and stated he is 'not MAGA.'
discover_titles: Elon Musk Regrets 2026 Midterm Spending: 'I Feel Pretty Foolish'
Musk States He Is 'Not MAGA' After Midterm Bets Fail
Billionaire Elon Musk Reflects on Costly 2026 Midterm Donations
spot: During an interview at The New York Times' DealBook Summit on Wednesday, billionaire Elon Musk admitted he feels 'pretty foolish' about spending hundreds of millions of dollars to assist Republican candidates in the 2026 midterms. Musk also declared he is 'not MAGA' and described his political beliefs as 'quite moderate.'
content_html:
Key Developments

Billionaire Elon Musk revealed Wednesday that he feels "pretty foolish" after pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into supporting Republican candidates during the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking at The New York Times' DealBook Summit, the world's richest man—who previously served in President Trump's administration in 2025—also stated that he is "not MAGA" and views his political ideology as "quite moderate."'

Musk's massive political donations included transferring over $150 million to a super PAC supporting Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Texas. However, those financial bets largely failed to pay off. Democrats secured large majorities in both the House and Senate, while Paxton lost his race to Democratic candidate James Talarico. Furthermore, Democrats captured the Texas governor's office, marking a significant political shift in the state where Musk bases major operations for SpaceX and Tesla.

According to Musk, his primary objective was to help Republicans retain their Senate majority to prevent single-party control of the presidency and Congress in 2029, a strategy he acknowledged failed. Reflecting on the outcome, Musk told interviewer Andrew Ross Sorkin that if he could rewind the clock, he would have spent less money. While addressing past controversial remarks and his previous "dark MAGA" persona from 2024, Musk clarified that he does not have a blind adherence to Republican policies and sees both positives and negatives in both major political parties.

Key Takeaways

  • Financial Regret: Musk spent hundreds of millions supporting GOP midterm candidates, including a $150 million investment in Texas, but stated he now feels "pretty foolish" after Republican defeats.
  • Political Stance: Musk explicitly stated he is "not MAGA," describing his political beliefs as "quite moderate" and emphasizing a desire for checks and balances.
  • Election Fallout: Democrats secured majorities in the House and Senate, defeating high-profile GOP candidates backed by Musk and shifting the political landscape in Texas.

Why It Matters

The remarks signal a notable shift in tone for Musk, who was a prominent financial backer of the Trump campaign in 2024 and led the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency. The failure of his costly 2026 midterm investments highlights the limits of billionaire spending in swaying voter outcomes, particularly in key battleground states like Texas. Musk's pivot to describing himself as a moderate seeking checks and balances provides insight into his evolving political alignment following major Democratic victories in Congress and state races.
